series: Why we stop doing things we know are good for us, Reason #20 (just today)
hook: Skipping just today, twice a week, costs you 104 days a year.

gate.goal_link: any big goal built from regular sessions (guitar, running, a side project) loses months to skips that each felt harmless
gate.mechanism: narrow choice bracketing: each skip is judged as one isolated day, so the cost of the repeated pattern is never seen (Read, Loewenstein & Rabin 1999, 'choice bracketing'; said as 'researchers call this choice bracketing', no numbers attributed)
gate.universal: saying 'just today' to a habit you care about

frame.obstacle: each skip feels like one free day
frame.cost: 2 skips a week = 104 days a year (arithmetic, not a study)
frame.fix: before skipping ask 'would I be okay skipping this every week?'; if not, do the 10-minute version (the 45-minute plan stays, owner rule)

hooks_considered.line: Skipping just today, twice a week, costs you 104 days a year.
hooks_considered.checks: hard truth Y, gap Y, muted Y (1 vs 104 bars), sendable Y, payoff Y

hooks_considered.line: 'Just today' is the most expensive thing you say.
Your goal doesn't die. It gets skipped to death.
Two skips a week. Three months a year.
